display.title: Sefirah and Respect: Rabbi Akiva's Students and Ahavas Yisroel
display.summary_short: Why there is no music during Sefirah, what we learn from Rabbi Akiva's students, and how respect, Ahavas Yisroel and achdus bring Moshiach closer.
display.summary_long: A Sefirah talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi explains why the program begins without music: during the days of Sefirah we remember the plague in which thousands of Rabbi Akiva's students died because they did not give each other proper respect. Each year we ask whether we practice the mitzvah of respect properly: honoring father and mother, honoring teachers and rabbis, and respecting friends by looking at them with a good eye, avoiding quarrels and making up after a disagreement, as the Mishnah says, 'love peace and pursue peace'. If the punishment for disrespect was so great, the reward for respect is surely greater. Ahavas Yisroel and achdus, together with Torah and mitzvos, are the answer to our cry of 'Ad masai', how long until Moshiach. Soldiers of Tzivos Hashem should set the example in davening, tzedakah, peace and good manners, so that other children will want to follow.
display.lesson: Respect and love every Jew, especially during Sefirah, and set an example that others will want to follow.
